facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin

support_spans: multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
contradict_spans: AFP, CEA, CA19-9, and CA125 were within normal limits
concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with melanin pigments, and positivity for melanoma markers support this diagnosis.

support_spans: multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver

concepts.why: The presence of melanin pigments and positivity for melanoma markers in the liver masses support this rare diagnosis.

rationales.F10: Epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments suggest melanoma.
rationales.F11: Diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E is highly indicative of melanoma.
rationales.F08: Negative HBsAg and anti-HCV reduce the likelihood of liver disease, but do not specifically rule out melanoma metastasis or primary hepatic melanoma.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E, along with the clinical presentation of multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver, decided it.
